title: Integer Types, Ranges and Signedness
learningObjectives: Explain the central rules behind integer types, ranges and signedness in C.
Identify the relevant types, declarations, operators or library facilities.
Trace a worked example and explain its result.
Recognize common mistakes, portability concerns and unsafe assumptions.
Apply the concept in a small program and test normal and boundary cases.

understand.concept: C integer types include _Bool, char, short, int, long and long long, each with signed and unsigned forms where permitted. Their ranges depend on implementation characteristics. Signed overflow is undefined behaviour; unsigned arithmetic is performed modulo one more than the maximum representable value.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the correct integer type requires considering range, arithmetic behaviour and interfaces. Signedness bugs can affect comparisons, loops, array indexing and input validation.
understand.analogy: Think of a type as a contract that describes what kind of value an object can hold and which operations make sense for it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only an introduction; C types also determine representation, conversions, alignment and constraints.

explain.narrative:
C integer types include _Bool, char, short, int, long and long long, each with signed and unsigned forms where permitted. Their ranges depend on implementation characteristics. Signed overflow is undefined behaviour; unsigned arithmetic is performed modulo one more than the maximum representable value.

Choosing the correct integer type requires considering range, arithmetic behaviour and interfaces. Signedness bugs can affect comparisons, loops, array indexing and input validation.

When reviewing code, identify the declared types first, then trace conversions and the exact expression being evaluated. Compile with warnings enabled and test boundary values. Do not rely on assumptions about another compiler or machine.

examples.title: A second case
examples.code: int maximum = INT_MAX;\n/* Do not compute maximum + 1 in signed int. */\nprintf("%d\\n", maximum);
examples.explanation: Adding one to INT_MAX in signed int would overflow and has undefined behaviour; use a wider or otherwise suitable representation after checking its range.

practise.guidedTask: Use limits.h to display the ranges of int, unsigned int, long and long long. Write a checked increment function that refuses to overflow.
practise.independentTask: Review a loop that compares an int index with size_t length. Correct the signed/unsigned comparison and explain why the types differ.
hints: Unsigned arithmetic wraps modulo the type's range plus one.
Check bounds before performing arithmetic that may overflow.
Avoid mixing signed and unsigned values without an explicit reason.
